channel.title: Phi Tran — Blog
channel.description: Notes on protocol internals, infrastructure decisions and verification.

item.title: Half the portfolio advice I checked did not survive verification
item.description: I ran twenty-five claims about engineer portfolios through adversarial verification. Eleven died — and almost all of them were the statistics people quote most confidently.

item.title: Nobody can tell you who viewed your GitHub profile
item.description: There is no LinkedIn-style visitor list, the view counter badge cannot identify anyone, and the tracking-pixel trick does not work. Here is what is actually measurable.

item.title: A multisig protects against a stolen key, not against every signer being shown the same lie
item.description: Threshold signing assumes signers are approving different views of the same truth. When the interface is compromised, M-of-N approves the same forgery M times.

item.title: The gateway, not the node, is what makes self-hosting trustworthy
item.description: Running your own node fixes cost, privacy and latency. It does not fix the failure that actually hurts, because your node can lag too.

item.title: Subgraph for the read side, custom indexer for the money path
item.description: A rule I arrived at after building both. The deciding factor is not query convenience — it is what happens to your balances during a reorg.
